title: Albania Road Trip Itinerary: 7 Days from Tirana Airport (Plus a 10-Day Version)
metaTitle: Albania Road Trip Itinerary: 7 & 10 Days by Car
metaDescription: A day-by-day Albania road trip itinerary for 7 or 10 days from Tirana airport: Berat, Gjirokastër, Ksamil, the Riviera and Theth. Plan your route now.
excerpt: A practical day-by-day Albania road trip loop starting and ending at Tirana airport: Berat, Gjirokastër, Ksamil and the Riviera in 7 days, plus Shkodër and Theth in 10.
html:
The best Albania road trip itinerary for 7 days is a loop from Tirana airport through Berat and Gjirokastër to Ksamil, then back north along the Albanian Riviera via the Llogara Pass and Vlorë. It combines two UNESCO-listed towns, the Ionian beaches and some of the most scenic coastal driving in Europe, without spending all day behind the wheel. With 10 days you can add the north: Shkodër and the mountain village of Theth.

Before you go: planning basics

  • Best time: May, June and September offer warm weather, swimmable sea and fewer crowds. July and August are hot and busy on the coast. Theth is best from late spring to early autumn.
  • Which car: a compact car is fine for the 7-day loop. For the 10-day version with Theth, or with a family and luggage, consider an SUV.
  • Driving times: app estimates are often optimistic on mountain and coastal roads. Allow extra time for photo stops and lunch.
  • Rules of the road: read our guide to driving in Albania before you set off.

7-day route at a glance

DayRouteApprox. driving timeOvernight
1Tirana airport – Tirana20–30 minTirana
2Tirana – BeratAbout 2 hBerat
3Berat – Gjirokastër3–3.5 hGjirokastër
4Gjirokastër – Blue Eye – KsamilAbout 2 h plus stopsKsamil or Sarandë
5Butrint and Ksamil beachesShort drivesKsamil or Sarandë
6Ksamil – Riviera – Llogara Pass – Vlorë3.5–4.5 h plus stopsVlorë or Dhërmi
7Vlorë – Durrës – Tirana airport2–2.5 hFlight home

Day-by-day itinerary

Day 1: Arrive at Tirana airport and explore Tirana

Collect your car at Tirana International Airport and drive the short distance into the capital. Spend the afternoon around Skanderbeg Square, the National History Museum and the Pyramid of Tirana, then have dinner in the lively Blloku district. If you land late, keep the evening simple. Check that your hotel has parking, as street parking in central Tirana is limited.

Day 2: Tirana to Berat

Drive south for about two hours to Berat, known as the "city of a thousand windows". Walk up to the castle quarter, where people still live inside the old walls, and enjoy the view over the Osum River. In the late afternoon, stroll through the Mangalem and Gorica quarters as the white Ottoman-era houses glow in the evening light. Park in the lower town, as the lanes up to the castle are steep and narrow.

Day 3: Berat to Gjirokastër

Head south towards Gjirokastër, a drive of roughly three hours through river valleys and hills. Gjirokastër, another UNESCO-listed town, is famous for its stone-roofed houses and its large hilltop castle. Visit the castle and the old bazaar, and if you have time, one of the traditional fortified houses open to visitors. The cobbled streets are very steep, so an automatic car makes life easier here if you are not used to hill starts.

Day 4: Gjirokastër to Ksamil via the Blue Eye

On the way to the coast, stop at the Blue Eye (Syri i Kaltër), a deep natural spring of intensely blue water surrounded by forest. It is a short walk from the car park, and the water is cold all year. Continue over the hills to Sarandë and then south to Ksamil, where you can spend the late afternoon swimming in the clear Ionian Sea.

Day 5: Butrint and the beaches of Ksamil

Visit the ancient site of Butrint early in the morning, before the heat and the tour groups. This UNESCO site combines Greek, Roman, Byzantine and Venetian remains in a beautiful lagoon setting. Spend the rest of the day on Ksamil's beaches, or take a small boat to the islands just offshore. In high season, park once and walk rather than moving the car around.

Day 6: The Albanian Riviera to Vlorë

This is the most scenic driving day. Head north along the coast road, stopping at Lukovë, Borsh with its long pebble beach, and the small fortress at Porto Palermo. Have lunch in Himarë, then continue past Dhërmi and climb the hairpins of the Llogara Pass for wide views over the sea. Descend through pine forest to Vlorë. If you prefer to stay by the beach, spend the night in Dhërmi or Himarë instead. Our guide to Albanian Riviera beaches by car covers every stop in detail.

Day 7: Vlorë to Tirana airport via Durrës

Drive north on the main road to Durrës, Albania's main port, and visit the Roman amphitheatre near the old town before the short final drive to the airport. If you have a flight in the late afternoon or evening, this day is comfortable. For an early flight, consider spending the last night in Durrës or near the airport.

The 10-day version: add Shkodër and Theth

With three extra days you can add the north, where the Albanian Alps offer a complete contrast to the coast. Follow days 1 to 6 above, then continue:

DayRouteApprox. driving timeOvernight
7Vlorë – Durrës – Shkodër3.5–4 hShkodër
8Shkodër – Theth2.5–3 hTheth
9Hiking around ThethNoneTheth
10Theth – Tirana airportAbout 4–4.5 hFlight home

Day 7: Vlorë to Shkodër

Drive north past Durrës and Tirana to Shkodër. Climb to Rozafa Castle for views over Lake Shkodër and the rivers, and enjoy the pedestrian street in the town centre in the evening.

Day 8: Shkodër to Theth

The road to Theth climbs over a mountain pass with spectacular views. It is now paved but narrow and winding, so drive slowly and allow plenty of time. Fill up with fuel in Shkodër, as there are no petrol stations in the mountains. Read our guide to Theth and Valbona by car for practical details.

Day 9: A day in Theth

Leave the car at your guesthouse and hike. Popular options are the walk to the Blue Eye of Theth, the Grunas waterfall and the old lock-in tower in the village. Fit hikers can tackle the trail over the pass to Valbona.

Day 10: Back to Tirana airport

Drive back down to Shkodër and continue south to the airport. Leave early: mountain roads take time, and you do not want to rush to catch a flight.

Alternative: a shorter 5-day loop

Short on time? Combine Tirana, Berat and the Riviera: airport to Berat (day 1), Berat to Vlorë and Dhërmi (day 2), a beach day (day 3), Himarë and the coast (day 4), then back to the airport (day 5). For even shorter stays, our list of day trips from Tirana by car has plenty of ideas.

Practical tips for your Albania road trip

  • Book accommodation with parking, especially in Ksamil, Berat and Gjirokastër.
  • Start driving days early to avoid the midday heat and arrive before dark.
  • Carry some cash in lek for small guesthouses, parking and roadside cafés.
  • Think about insurance: Super CDW removes the excess, which is reassuring on narrow coastal and mountain roads.
  • Visiting a neighbouring country? Corfu is across the water from Sarandë, and Montenegro is close to Shkodër. Taking the car across a border requires a cross-border permit arranged in advance.

faq.question: Is 7 days enough for an Albania road trip?
faq.answer: Seven days is enough for a rewarding loop covering Tirana, Berat, Gjirokastër, Ksamil, Butrint and the Riviera, with one or two relaxed beach days. You will not see the northern mountains, though. With 10 days you can add Shkodër and Theth, and with two weeks you can travel at a slower pace.

faq.question: Should I do the Albania road trip clockwise or anticlockwise?
faq.answer: Both directions work. Going south inland via Berat and Gjirokastër and returning along the coast means you end with the Riviera and arrive at the beaches after some sightseeing. The reverse puts the beaches first, which suits travellers who want to relax straight after the flight and leave the sightseeing for later in the trip.

faq.question: Do I need a 4x4 for an Albania road trip?
faq.answer: No. The main 7-day route uses paved roads throughout, and a normal compact or mid-size car is perfectly fine. The road to Theth is now paved too, but it is steep and winding, so an SUV is more comfortable there. A higher car also helps on gravel tracks leading to some remote beaches.

faq.question: How much driving is there on a 7-day Albania itinerary?
faq.answer: The full loop covers roughly 700 to 800 km depending on detours. Most driving days are between two and four hours, plus stops. The Riviera day from Ksamil to Vlorë is the longest in practice, because the road is winding and you will want to stop at beaches and viewpoints.
